stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. An $R$-module $Q$ is injective if and only if in every
commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathfrak{a} \ar[d] \ar[r] &  Q \\
R \ar@{-->}[ru]
}
$$
for $\mathfrak{a} \subset R$ an ideal, the dotted arrow exists.
hypotheses: R a ring, Q an R-module.
conclusions: Q is injective if and only if any R-linear map from an ideal a⊂R to Q extends to R→Q.

reason: The Baer lifting criterion is explicitly identified with the corresponding injectivity equivalence in the cited More on Algebra lemma, which supplies a non-circular elementary proof.
